title: Context-boundary cache thrash causing tokens/sec collapse across fleet
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers (notably BrightArc Health on Dedicated and a Private deploy) have reported sudden drops in tokens/sec and increased TTFT spikes during multi-model fanout traffic. Root cause investigation points to aggressive context-boundary invalidation combined with adapter/model-switch prefetches that cause a KV-cache refill storm. This leads to worker CPU saturation and downstream throttling, manifesting as sustained tokens/sec collapse for 30–120s bursts.

Repro steps observed: 1) Long session with mixed model variants (small+large) hits router affinity boundary. 2) Router triggers model-swap prefetch for large variant; prefetch issues cause simultaneous KV cache evictions. 3) Multiple workers concurrently attempt to rebuild KV shards causing elevated disk/PCIe egress and CPU in decoding queues. 4) Throughput drops and tail TTFT increases; streaming first-byte latency remains high for affected sessions.

Why this is urgent: Enterprise SLAs are breached for customers on Dedicated and Private; hosted customers see transient degradation when cross-tenant model mixing spikes. Business impact: revenue-sensitive customers reporting failed requests and customer support escalations (BrightArc Health SLA incident 2026-03-09).

Investigation artfacts: Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft-team/context-boundary-dd?view=bs (queries: tokens/sec by model, kv-cache miss rate). Traces: Jaeger trace set linked in incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-03-kv-thrash. Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/142 (WIP).

Hypothesis: The simultaneous prefetch + cache invalidation at context boundaries causes pathological rebuild behavior. Current backoff for prefetch is too aggressive (no jitter) and eviction policy is LRU-only which mispredicts cross-session reuse.

Temporary mitigations applied (2026-03-10 18:30 UTC): - Deployed hotpatch to reduce concurrent prefetch window from 16 -> 4 per-worker (quick roll). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3742. - Enabled KV-prefetch circuit-breaker that rejects new prefetches when miss-rate exceeds threshold (configured conservatively). - Per-customer temporary routing rule to pin BrightArc to a warm pool for the remainder of business hours.

Observed results: Immediate reduction in 95p TTFT from 3.1s -> 1.4s for affected sessions; tokens/sec recovered to ~85% baseline in canary region. Some degradation remains for high-fanout synthetic tests; further fix required.

Planned permanent changes: 1) Implement adaptive eviction policy: frequency-aware LRU + workload hinting to protect cross-session shared KV shards. 2) Add randomized jitter and exponential backoff to prefetch attempts; include a global in-flight prefetch quota per-node. 3) Add lightweight pre-warm step during rollouts to avoid cold-surge. 4) Update router to prefer model-stability lanes for long sessions (i.e., reduce mid-session model-switching unless explicitly requested).

Rollout plan: - Merge kernel/runtime changes to a feature branch -> safety tests (unit + e2e perf). - Canary rollout to 3 nodes in hosted-us-east-1 for 60 minutes; monitor tokens/sec, TTFT, error-rate. - Expand to Dedicated pools for affected customers (BrightArc) behind customer-aware feature flag. - Full fleet rollout in runtime-2.4 patch if metrics stable. Rollback criteria: tokens/sec < 90% baseline for >5 minutes OR error-rate >0.5% above baseline.

Acceptance criteria: 1) sustained tokens/sec within 95% of baseline during synthetic fanout test (30m window). 2) 95p TTFT improvement vs pre-fix (target <1.6s). 3) No increase in 5xxs or stream termination errors beyond baseline.

Next steps & owners: - Tomás Rivera: complete adaptive eviction POC (due 2026-03-13). - Priya Kapoor: add backoff + jitter to prefetch logic and write unit tests (due 2026-03-13). - SRE (Jared Liu): prepare canary config and monitoring alerts for tokens/sec regressions (due 2026-03-12). - CS (Maya Chen): coordinate BrightArc rollback window and comms (in progress).

Notes: This ticket will be linked to follow-on performance tasks and an incident retrospective doc. We should also run a capacity simulation for mixed-fanout workloads as part of Optimize recommendations.
